Consult Summary:
- Patient presents with acute chest pressure started a few hours ago while gardening, with nausea, sweating, and shortness of breath; symptoms persist.
- Concern raised for acute coronary syndrome; ambulance to be arranged; patient has an aspirin allergy that must be communicated to EMS/hospital.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute chest discomfort with potential acute coronary syndrome.
  - Timeline and associated symptoms: Onset a couple of hours ago during gardening (not during strenuous activity); diffuse mid-chest pressure with radiation to left arm and shoulder; accompanying nausea, sweating, and shortness of breath; palpitations reported.
  - Systems review: Chest pain with left arm/shoulder involvement; nausea; diaphoresis; shortness of breath; no vomiting.
  - Social history, medications, and examination findings: Smokes ~10 cigarettes/day for ~15 years; history of hypertension; overweight; family history of heart disease (father died of MI around age 60; mother with heart problems); alcohol ~7–8 pints/week; lives alone; works as sushi shop owner. No vitals or physical exam findings documented.
  - Specialist/allied health review or differential diagnosis: Ambulance/EMS to assess; ECG to be performed; differential includes acute coronary syndrome; diagnosis not yet confirmed.

Issue 2:
- Aspirin allergy.
  - Timeline and associated symptoms: Allergic reaction described as swelling; not life-threatening; no dose/route/frequency provided.
  - Systems review/medications: Allergy to aspirin; no other allergies.
  - Social history/education plan: Doctor advised hospital to be informed of aspirin allergy; aspirin may still be considered depending on clinical judgment.
  - Plan: Communicate aspirin allergy to EMS/hospital; management decisions to be made by ambulance/hospital team.

Issue 3:
- Cardiovascular risk factors and social history relevant to potential cardiac event.
  - Timeline: Not time-based; risk factors present.
  - Systems review/medications: Hypertension; overweight; smoking; family history of heart disease; alcohol use.
  - Social history: Lives alone; occupation as restaurant owner; active smoking history; weekly alcohol intake.
  - Examination/plan: No physical exam or vitals recorded in the encounter; actions focus on urgent EMS evaluation.

Medications:
- None documented.

Allergies:
- Aspirin allergy (allergic reaction with swelling; dose/route/frequency not documented).

Past Medical History:
- Hypertension.
- Overweight.
- Not diabetes (per patient report).
- Family history of heart disease (father died of MI around age 60; mother with heart problems).

Social History:
- Lives alone.
- Smokes ~10 cigarettes/day for ~15 years.
- Alcohol: ~7–8 pints per week.
- Occupation: Sushi shop owner.

Preventative History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- No vitals or examination findings documented.

Plan:
- Ambulance to be called; EMS to perform ECG and assess; potential hospital transfer based on ECG and clinical assessment.
- Doctor will stay online with patient until EMS arrives and will hand over to hospital team after EMS assessment.
- Inform hospital about aspirin allergy; aspirin consideration to be determined by clinical team.
- Front door access noted (for EMS) per household safety.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements: Vitals, explicit medication reconciliation, and objective physical examination findings/ECG results not available in transcript.
- Internal conflicts: Conflict noted regarding patient age estimation; clinician estimated ~50s, patient stated around 60.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some back-and-forth and minor repetition; no major inaudible segments.
